title: Keyflow Spacing Engine — MuseScore-Inspired Improvements
description:
Incremental improvements to the Keyflow chart engraver's horizontal spacing engine, inspired by MuseScore 4's algorithms. Addresses cramped measures in dense sections, chord symbol collisions for long extensions, and lack of duration-proportional beat spacing.

Key additions:
- Power-law duration-to-space formula for proportional beat spacing
- Spring-based justification at both measure and beat level
- Improved chord symbol collision prevention with NON_KERNING semantics
- Squeeze algorithm for graceful overflow handling
- Configurable spacing density/slope parameters

Reference: memory/MuseScoreSpacingReport.md

Applies to all layout modes (paginated, continuous, snippet).
close_reason: Closed

title: US-001: Add duration stretch formula to segment spacing
description:
As a chart reader, I want beat spacing within measures to reflect note duration so that longer notes naturally get more horizontal space than shorter notes.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Implement `duration_stretch(ticks, quarter_ticks, slope) -> f64` using `slope.powf((ticks / quarter_ticks).log2())`
- [ ] Implement `natural_width(ticks, spatium, slope, density) -> f64` returning `base_quarter_width * stretch / density`
- [ ] Default `base_quarter_width = 3.5 * spatium` (MuseScore standard)
- [ ] Default `slope = 1.2`, `density = 1.0`
- [ ] Add `spacing_slope: f64` and `spacing_density: f64` fields to `LayoutParams` in `config/layout_params.rs`
- [ ] Unit tests: quarter=1.0 stretch, half≈1.2, whole≈1.44, eighth≈0.83 (at slope=1.2)
- [ ] Integration: `compute_x_positions()` in `segment_list.rs` uses duration-based natural widths for ChordRest segments instead of uniform spacing
- [ ] Create new module `engraver-proto/src/engraver/layout/chart/spacing.rs` for the formulas
- [ ] `cargo test -p keyflow-proto --lib` passes
- [ ] `cargo test -p engraver-proto --lib` passes
- [ ] Visual PDF verification with Belief chart: beats within measures show proportional spacing

## Technical Context
- MuseScore formula: `pow(slope, log2(duration_ratio))` where `duration_ratio = ticks / quarter_note_ticks`
- See memory/MuseScoreSpacingReport.md Section 2 for full details
- Insertion point: `compute_x_positions()` in `segment_list.rs`
- `Segment` struct already has `ticks` and `stretch` fields
- Constants go in `constants.rs`
close_reason: Closed

title: US-002: Implement spring model for beat-level justification
description:
As a chart reader, I want remaining space within a measure (after natural widths are computed) to be distributed proportionally via springs so that longer beats expand more than shorter beats.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Implement `Spring { spring_const: f64, width: f64, pre_tension: f64 }` struct in `spacing.rs`
- [ ] Implement `stretch_segments_to_width(springs, extra_width)` using MuseScore's equilibrium-force algorithm: sort by pre_tension, iterate to find force, apply `force / spring_const` as new width
- [ ] `spring_const = 1.0 / duration_stretch` for each beat segment (stiffer for short notes)
- [ ] After computing natural widths in a measure, if total < measure width, distribute excess via springs
- [ ] Unit tests: given springs with different constants, verify proportional distribution
- [ ] Visual verification: in Belief chart, Breakdown measures with `Dm7_8 C_8 Dm7 ///` show 8th notes narrower than quarter/dotted-half
- [ ] `cargo test -p keyflow-proto --lib` passes
- [ ] `cargo test -p engraver-proto --lib` passes

## Technical Context
- MuseScore algorithm: sort springs by preTension ascending, accumulate 1/k and widths, solve force = total / sum(1/k), apply new_width = force / k
- See memory/MuseScoreSpacingReport.md Section 7 for pseudocode
- Builds on the `spacing.rs` module and duration_stretch from US-001
- Key insight: shorter durations have higher spring_const (stiffer), so they expand less
close_reason: Closed

title: US-003: Implement spring model for measure-level justification
description:
As a chart reader, I want measures on a full line to be stretched to fill the line width using springs so that measures with longer notes expand more than measures with short notes.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Replace current weight-proportional distribution in `distribute_measure_widths_with_mins()` in `measure_layout.rs` with spring-based justification
- [ ] Each measure's spring constant derived from its total duration stretch (sum of segment stretches)
- [ ] Reuse `stretch_segments_to_width()` from US-002 at the measure level
- [ ] Short systems (fewer than max measures) do NOT justify — leave ragged (MuseScore's lastSystemFillLimit concept)
- [ ] Add `last_system_fill_limit: f64` to `LayoutParams` (default 0.3)
- [ ] Unit tests: 4 measures with different content get different widths; final system with 2/4 measures stays ragged
- [ ] Visual verification: full lines in Belief chart look evenly distributed; final line of each section not stretched
- [ ] `cargo test -p keyflow-proto --lib` passes
- [ ] `cargo test -p engraver-proto --lib` passes

## Technical Context
- See memory/MuseScoreSpacingReport.md Sections 7 and 9 for justification and last-system logic
- Current code: `distribute_measure_widths_with_mins()` in `measure_layout.rs` uses weight-proportional distribution
- The spring model replaces simple weight distribution with force-equilibrium distribution
- lastSystemFillLimit: if curWidth/targetWidth < 0.3, don't justify (leave ragged)
close_reason: Closed

title: US-004: Improve chord symbol collision prevention
description:
As a chart reader, I want chord symbols to never overlap each other, especially for long names like Cmaj7#11 or Dm7b5/Ab.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Chord symbols use NON_KERNING semantics: adjacent chord symbols always maintain minimum padding, never compress
- [ ] Minimum chord-to-chord padding = font_size * 0.35 (increase from current 0.25)
- [ ] When a chord symbol's measured width would collide with the next chord's position, expand the measure's minimum width to accommodate
- [ ] Push chord notation (''C) reserves space for both the push indicator and the chord name
- [ ] When hide-repeated-chord removes a chord name, the space previously occupied is reclaimed (gap closed)
- [ ] Update `measure_pass.rs` collision detection to account for new duration-based segment positions (not uniform)
- [ ] Visual verification: Belief chart Breakdown section has no chord symbol overlaps
- [ ] `cargo test -p keyflow-proto --lib` passes
- [ ] `cargo test -p engraver-proto --lib` passes

## Technical Context
- Current collision detection: `measure_pass.rs` lines 559-678 computes min_width from chord widths
- Current min gap: font_size * 0.25 (line 453) — increase to 0.35
- MuseScore rule: Harmony vs Harmony = NON_KERNING (never compress, always full gap + padding)
- MuseScore rule: Harmony vs BarLine = ALLOW_COLLISION (chord can sit over barline)
- See memory/MuseScoreSpacingReport.md Section 10 for chord symbol rules
- Must account for new duration-based positions when calculating collisions
close_reason: Closed

title: US-005: Implement squeeze algorithm for overflow handling
description:
As a chart reader, I want measures that are too wide for the available space to gracefully compress rather than overflowing or clipping.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Implement two-phase squeeze in spacing.rs:
  - Phase 1: reduce squeeze_factor by 0.2 steps AND stretch_reduction by 0.33 steps, recompute spacing each iteration
  - Phase 2: scale segment widths directly if Phase 1 fails (brute-force)
- [ ] squeeze_factor multiplies all padding values and segment spacing
- [ ] stretch_reduction multiplies the duration-based natural width
- [ ] Squeeze activates automatically when a measure's content exceeds its allocated width
- [ ] System-level squeeze: when all measures on a line exceed target width, squeeze the entire line
- [ ] Unit tests: a measure with excessive content squeezes to fit without overflow
- [ ] Visual verification: dense Breakdown measures in Belief chart compress gracefully
- [ ] cargo test -p keyflow-proto --lib passes
- [ ] cargo test -p engraver-proto --lib passes

## Technical Context
- MuseScore constants: STRETCH_REDUCTION_STEP = 0.33, SQUEEZE_STEP = 0.2
- Phase 1 loop: while (curWidth > targetWidth && squeezeFactor > 0) { recompute; squeezeFactor -= 0.2; stretchReduction -= 0.33 }
- Phase 2: direct segment width scaling in 0.05 steps (allows collisions as last resort)
- See memory/MuseScoreSpacingReport.md Section 8 for full algorithm
- Must parameterize spacing.rs functions to accept squeeze_factor and stretch_reduction
close_reason: Closed

title: US-006: Enforce minimum measure width with duration scaling
description:
As a chart reader, I want every measure to have a minimum width that accounts for its time signature proportion so that pickup measures and short measures don't look too narrow.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Minimum measure width scales by time signature ratio: min_width * (measure_ticks / timesig_ticks) for partial measures
- [ ] After all spacing is computed, measures below minimum are stretched via the spring model from US-002
- [ ] min_measure_width remains configurable in LayoutParams (default 100pt)
- [ ] Unit tests: a 2/4 pickup measure gets half the minimum width of a 4/4 measure
- [ ] Visual verification: no measures in Belief chart appear cramped or narrower than readable
- [ ] cargo test -p keyflow-proto --lib passes
- [ ] cargo test -p engraver-proto --lib passes

## Technical Context
- MuseScore formula: if (m.ticks < m.timesig) then minWidth *= (m.ticks / m.timesig)
- After min enforcement, use stretchMeasureToTargetWidth (spring model) to expand
- See memory/MuseScoreSpacingReport.md Section 12 (Minimum Measure Width)
- Current: DEFAULT_MIN_MEASURE_WIDTH = 100.0 in constants.rs
close_reason: Closed

title: US-007: Apply improvements to continuous and snippet layout modes
description:
As a user, I want the spacing improvements to work consistently across paginated, continuous, and snippet rendering modes.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] layout_continuous() in mod.rs uses the same duration-stretch and spring justification as paginated
- [ ] Snippet mode uses natural widths (no justification stretching) with duration-based proportions
- [ ] Continuous mode handles infinite-width differently: no system-level squeeze, but beat-level duration spacing applies
- [ ] Unit tests: same measure produces consistent segment positions in paginated vs continuous mode (relative, not absolute)
- [ ] Visual verification: snippet output for a single measure shows proportional beat spacing
- [ ] cargo test -p keyflow-proto --lib passes
- [ ] cargo test -p engraver-proto --lib passes

## Technical Context
- Paginated: layout_paginated() in mod.rs lines 449-1191
- Continuous: layout_continuous() in mod.rs lines 1193-1632
- Snippet: uses ideal widths (90pt per weight unit) — replace with natural_width() from spacing.rs
- The spacing.rs functions should be layout-mode agnostic — each mode calls them with appropriate parameters
- Snippet: no squeeze, no justify — just natural widths
- Continuous: no system-level squeeze, but measure-level and beat-level spacing applies
close_reason: Closed

title: FTS-Macros Mapping System Implementation
description:
Build a sample-accurate, self-contained mapping system for fts-macros that enables macro parameters to control other plugin FX parameters without requiring the fts-control extension to be running.

**Architecture Pattern:** Source (macro param) → Mode (transformation) → Target (FX parameter)

**Key Features:**
- Sample-accurate real-time parameter control
- Mappings stored in plugin state (JSONL format)  
- Hot-reload support from fts-control without restart
- Cross-platform support (macOS, Windows, Linux)
- MVP: Macro → FX parameter mapping only
close_reason: Closed

Scope:
- REAPER actions for `Generate Keyflow Tracks` and `Export Keyflow Chart to MIDI`

- Marker/region/section parsing parity between live and offline paths
- Measure-accurate chart generation with reliable section boundaries and barlines
- Regression coverage using the Vienna chart and smaller fixtures

Why this exists:
- REAPER's native MIDI export does not preserve regions as MIDI markers
- live-only export is hard to test and slows iteration
- current chart generation still has section and measure correctness issues that need a tracked plan

   - Split nodes: create a parallel container, create sub-containers per lane, load blocks per lane
4. Use fx_chain().create_container() + set_routing_mode(Parallel) for split nodes

title: US-008: Implement scene switching for loaded rig in REAPER
description:

- DawBridge (signal-live/src/engine/daw_bridge.rs) applies diffs to REAPER

title: dawfile-reaper: Blazing-fast parser + extensible chunk architecture
description:
We need a major performance and architecture overhaul for `modules/dawfile/dawfile-reaper`.

Current measured baseline on `Goodness of God.RPP` (~418.82 MB):
- `parse_rpp_file`: ~40.3s
- typed conversion: ~0.53s

Goals:
1. Make parse throughput dramatically faster (target single-digit seconds for 400MB-class projects).
2. Keep type safety and round-trip fidelity.
3. Make adding new chunk support straightforward (automation, full item/take details, source variants, etc.).
4. Add stable query/index APIs (e.g. total item count, source inventory, envelope stats) without reparsing.

Scope:
- parser engine performance work
- typed decoding pipeline redesign
- memory and concurrency optimization
- extensible chunk-handler architecture
- test/benchmark/perf-gate infrastructure

Out of scope:
- changing external REAPER file format semantics
- lossy transforms that break round-trip fidelity
acceptance_criteria:
- A benchmark suite exists and tracks large-fixture parse + typed decode times.
- Large fixture parse time is reduced substantially from baseline (target <= 8s; stretch <= 4s on same machine/profile).
- Feature-extension architecture exists (new chunk parser can be added without touching core parser loop).
- Query/index APIs expose totals and inventories (items, takes, sources, plugins, envelopes) from parsed projects.
- CI enforces perf regression budgets and round-trip correctness checks.
close_reason: Outdated — closing to move forward

title: (EPIC) dawfile-reaper: structural performance optimization plan (single-pass first)
description: Create and execute a staged optimization program to maximize single-pass parser throughput and typed decode efficiency for large REAPER projects while preserving full typed fidelity. Keep parallel top-block parsing as optional fallback unless it beats single-pass on real fixtures.
acceptance_criteria:
- Clear phased plan with measurable KPIs exists as child beads.
- Every phase has correctness gates (audit + targeted tests).
- Parser/typed improvements preserve full decoded counts on Goodness fixture.
- Performance deltas are tracked before/after each phase.
close_reason: Completed all phased parser optimization beads (12.1-12.7) with perf telemetry, scanner/tokenization/fx optimizations, parallel gating, and regression guardrail tests.

title: Perf-Plan-01: stabilize benchmark + telemetry matrix
description: Standardize repeatable perf runs for parse and typed decode (small, medium, large fixtures). Track parse time, typed time, throughput, alloc calls/MB, and peak RSS with fixed run settings and reporting format.
acceptance_criteria: - Canonical benchmark command set documented and scripted.\n- Results include parse+typed time, throughput, alloc metrics, peak RSS.\n- Baselines captured for Goodness fixture and at least one tempo-heavy fixture.
notes: Added canonical perf script modules/dawfile/dawfile-reaper/scripts/perf_matrix.sh, added tracked perf artifacts docs/perf-runs/latest.{md,txt}, and updated docs/performance-baseline.md with command matrix + Goodness/tempo baseline metrics.
close_reason: Benchmark command set scripted, telemetry matrix outputs tracked (parse+typed, throughput, allocs, RSS), and baselines captured for Goodness + tempo fixture.

title: Perf-Plan-02: single-pass scanner hot-loop optimization
description: Optimize fast single-pass scanner internals (line classification, numeric parsing, token construction) to reduce per-line allocations and branch overhead while preserving parser semantics.
acceptance_criteria: - Parse alloc calls/MB reduced vs baseline.\n- No semantic regressions in parser equivalence tests.\n- Goodness fixture parse throughput improves measurably.
notes: Optimized scanner hot loop in fast_project.rs by: (1) removing clone-heavy quoted block-header param extraction (now moves tokens via iterator), and (2) eliminating redundant trim calls by using is_skippable_trimmed() in line loops. Validation: cargo check -p dawfile-reaper passes. Perf (rpp_perf, release, warmup 1, repeat 7) on Goodness fixture: parse_avg_s=0.2937, throughput=1425.97 MB/s, parse_alloc_calls_avg=4,355,602, parse_alloc_mb_avg=751.69. Previous baseline (2026-02-11 doc): parse throughput 1293.75 MB/s, parse_alloc_calls_avg=4,362,878, parse_alloc_mb_avg=752.15.
close_reason: Single-pass scanner hot loop optimized (fewer header-token clones + reduced redundant trim work), with measured parse allocation reduction and improved Goodness throughput in repeated release runs.

title: Perf-Plan-03: zero-copy token/line borrowing strategy
description: Introduce a staged borrowed-token representation (or equivalent span-based storage) so parser can defer/avoid String allocation for hot identifiers and raw lines; only materialize owned data when typed decode requires it.
acceptance_criteria: - Design and implementation behind safe migration path.\n- Significant reduction in parse allocation MB on large fixture.\n- Typed outputs remain identical for supported domains.
notes: Implemented staged raw-line representation: added RppBlockContent::RawLine(Box<str>) for fast parser non-structured lines, with lazy tokenization in Track/Item/Fx decode paths. This provides a safe migration path for deferred token materialization without changing external parse APIs. Validation: cargo check -p dawfile-reaper; cargo test fast_parser_matches_nom_small_project; cargo test --test full_project_audit (Goodness fixture) passed. Perf (rpp_perf release, warmup 1, repeat 5): Goodness parse_alloc_calls_avg=2,283,144 (was 4,362,878 baseline), parse_alloc_mb_avg=688.44 (was 752.15), parse_throughput=1697.89 MB/s.
close_reason: Added deferred raw-line tokenization path with significant parse allocation reduction and maintained typed decode parity on supported domains.

title: Perf-Plan-04: typed decode selective tokenization
description: Further reduce typed decode overhead by tokenizing only consumed lines/fields in Track/Item/Envelope/Marker paths. Keep unknown/raw lines preserved but non-tokenized where possible.
acceptance_criteria: - Typed alloc MB/calls reduced vs baseline.\n- Full decoded counts preserved on Goodness audit.\n- Domain decode profiler shows improved tracks_items/tracks_plugins slices.
notes: Implemented selective lazy tokenization in typed decode: Item::from_block now prefilters raw lines with should_parse_item_raw_line() and only tokenizes consumed fields; SOURCE non-MIDI FILE extraction only tokenizes FILE lines. Combined with RawLine parser path, unknown lines stay preserved but non-tokenized. Validation: full_project_audit counts unchanged on Goodness (tracks=702, items=988, midi_events=69854, markers/regions=24, tempo_points=3). rpp_perf release (repeat 5): typed_alloc_calls_avg=511,432 and typed_alloc_mb_avg=69.84 vs baseline 529,959 / 70.40. decode_domains release (repeat 5): tracks_items=0.0136s, tracks_plugins=0.0064s.
close_reason: Typed decode now tokenizes only consumed item/source lines with preserved output counts and lower typed allocation telemetry.

title: Perf-Plan-05: FX path deep optimization
description: Eliminate remaining FX-chain heavy allocations (plugin/container raw block materialization, envelope raw blocks, repeated header parsing) in block-based decode paths.
acceptance_criteria: - tracks_plugins decode time reduced in decode_domains profiler.\n- Typed FX coverage unchanged in audits/tests.\n- Raw preservation behavior documented and tested.
notes: Optimized FX decode path allocations by switching FxChain::from_block flattening to borrowed/owned Cow<str> lines, avoiding string materialization for RawLine and single-identifier token lines. Added regression test test_from_block_supports_rawline_fast_path. Domain profiler (decode_domains, repeat 5, Goodness): tracks_plugins improved 0.0064s -> 0.0048s, tracks_full 0.0174s -> 0.0144s. rpp_perf (repeat 5, Goodness full typed): typed_alloc_calls_avg=380,401 and typed_alloc_mb_avg=54.32 (previous 511,432 / 69.84).
close_reason: FX from_block path now avoids heavy line materialization with preserved coverage/tests and faster tracks_plugins decode.

title: Perf-Plan-06: optional parallel parse path tuning
description: Tune top-level parallel block parsing so it only activates when it outperforms single-pass on target fixtures; keep it feature-gated/fallback until proven.
acceptance_criteria: - Parallel path has clear enable criteria.\n- Demonstrated speedup on at least one fixture class before defaulting.\n- Single-pass remains default if parallel does not win.
notes: Tuned parallel parse activation controls in fast_project: RPP_FAST_TOP_BLOCK_PARALLEL supports off/on/auto with single-pass default. 'on' forces top-level parallel parse; 'auto' now intentionally routes to single-pass until fixture-class wins are proven. Added conservative internal criteria scaffolding for future auto enablement (top-block-heavy + file-size + thread-count). Measured on Goodness (typed summary, repeat 3): off parse_avg_s=0.3025 (1384.51 MB/s) vs on parse_avg_s=0.4170 (1004.38 MB/s), so single-pass remains default.
close_reason: Parallel path is now explicitly opt-in with clear criteria and measured non-win on Goodness; single-pass remains default.

- stroke() -> PaintScene::stroke()

- push_layer() / pop_layer() -> identical
- reset() -> identical

### One Gap: Scene::append()
The cached scene compositing pattern (scene.append(&cached, Some(transform))) has no PaintScene equivalent. anyrender has append_scene() but it takes anyrender::Scene, not vello::Scene. Options:
1. Keep scene_mut() as a Vello-specific escape hatch for the caching hot path only
2. Record the engraver output as anyrender::Scene instead of vello::Scene
3. Upstream a backend-agnostic scene append to anyrender

## Files to Modify

1. engraver-proto/src/engraver/renderer/scene_renderer.rs - Change VelloSceneRenderer to render through &mut impl PaintScene instead of &mut vello::Scene
2. engraver-proto/src/engraver/renderer/cursor_renderer.rs - Change signature from &mut Scene to &mut impl PaintScene (only uses fill/stroke)
3. keyflow-ui/src/chart_renderer.rs - Update ChartLayoutManager to use PaintScene for rendering, keep cached scene pattern via scene_mut()
4. fts-control/desktop/src/chart_graphics.rs - Already uses anyrender, just needs scene_mut() for append (currently broken without local fork patch)

- [ ] VelloSceneRenderer renders through PaintScene trait instead of direct vello::Scene
- [ ] cursor_renderer uses PaintScene trait methods

## Context
Discovered while fixing build errors - chart_graphics.rs calls painter.scene_mut() which only exists in the local anyrender fork (reference/anyrender), not upstream. Rather than patching, we should abstract away the vello dependency properly.

title: Rig Templates — Skeleton presets with block/module placeholders
description:
Implement a template system for rig presets. Templates define the structure of a rig (which modules, which block types in each module, block aliases, descriptions) without binding to specific plugins or parameter values. Users can:

1. Create templates that define block placeholders (type + alias + description)
2. Create new presets from templates (inheriting the structure, then assigning real plugins)
3. Share templates across instrument types (guitar, vocals, etc.)
4. View placeholder blocks as grayed-out in the grid until assigned

## Key Concepts
- **RigTemplate**: Top-level template containing module templates + standalone block placeholders
- **ModuleTemplate**: A module slot with block type placeholders (not real plugins)
- **BlockPlaceholder**: A block type + optional alias + description, no plugin binding
- **Template instantiation**: Creating a real Preset from a template, with empty blocks ready to be filled

## Data Model Additions
- `Block` gets `alias: Option<String>` and `description: Option<String>` fields
- New `RigTemplate` type with `Vec<ModuleTemplate>` and `Vec<BlockPlaceholder>`
- New `ModuleTemplate` type with `module_type`, `name`, `description`, `Vec<BlockPlaceholder>`
- New `BlockPlaceholder` type with `block_type`, `alias`, `description`, `order`
- Template instantiation function: `RigTemplate` → `Preset` (with empty blocks)

## Built-in Templates
- Guitar Rig Template (Source, Dynamics, Special, Drive, Volume, Pre-FX, Amp/Cab, Modulation, Time, Motion, Mastering)
- Vocal Rig Template (Rescue, Correction, Tonal, Modulation, Time)

## UI Requirements
- Template browser/selector when creating new presets
- Grayed-out placeholder blocks in the grid (visually distinct from assigned blocks)
- Block alias and description shown in the detail/property panel
- Template editor for creating/editing templates

Reach practical feature parity between the Rust generic chunk API and ReaTeam_RPP-Parser.lua, while preserving existing typed adapters (ReaperProject/FxChain/FxTree) and adding compatibility-grade behavior for read/mutate/write workflows.

Scope
- Generic RToken/RNode/RChunk parity semantics
- Query/mutation API parity (name/filter/range/copy/remove/parent behavior)
- Stringification and quoting parity
- NOTES multiline pipe handling parity
- GUID strip parity options
- Read/parse input mode parity and error behavior
- Dedicated parity tests against Lua behavior

Out of scope
- Replacing existing typed project/fx parsers
- Non-REAPER format extensions
acceptance_criteria: All parity child tasks complete; parity test suite passes; example workflows (read, mutate, write) match Lua parser behavior on representative RPP/RFXCHAIN fixtures.
close_reason: All parity beads completed with API facade, behavior parity updates, bridge hardening, fixture tests, and migration docs
